key_insight: A surrogate-assisted Bayesian inverse-design workflow can efficiently tune an all-oxide TPV emitter to achieve a high, narrowband peak emission aligned with the target bandgap.
engineering_relevance: Using ITO/Al2O3 on sapphire avoids many high-temperature degradation issues of metal-based emitters while improving spectral selectivity and thermal robustness for thermophotovoltaic systems.
method: Generated FDTD emission spectra by varying layer thicknesses and grating period.
Trained ExtraTrees surrogate models on spectral/FOM data.
Ran Bayesian optimization with a penalty on peak emission, then validated the best design with FDTD.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimization over a peak-emission constraint (E_peak > 0.90) while minimizing FWHM and maximizing in-band fraction, followed by FDTD validation of the predicted optimal structure.
watch_item: Performance is tied to surrogate accuracy and the final design space explored, so fabrication tolerances and temperature-dependent material-property shifts may reduce real-device agreement.
paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Inverse Design and Temperature-Dependent Electrothermal Analysis of an All-Oxide Narrowband Thermophotovoltaic Emitter
